The central maximum is white, with the colours of the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum at the edges.

Violet is the closest to the centre of the central maximum, because it has the shortest wavelength, therefore it is diffracted the least.

Red is the farthest from the centre of the central maximum, because it has the longest wavelength, so it is diffracted the most.

Secondary maxima are in the colours of the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum from violet (closest to centre) to red (farthest from centre).
